findings.title: Provenance validation accepts non-reproducible observations and impossible dates
findings.what: Observation field/value citations are optional, and asOf is checked only with a digit-shape regex. Consequently source-only claims and impossible dates such as 2026-99-99 pass validation, so evidence cannot necessarily be located or temporally reproduced. The contract test explicitly blesses the source-only shape and tests only a timestamp-shaped invalid date.
findings.fix: Require a non-empty field and scalar value for claim-bearing observations, and validate asOf by parsing it and round-tripping to the exact YYYY-MM-DD value; update the contract tests accordingly.
findings.acceptance: Tests reject an observation lacking field/value and reject 2026-99-99 and 2026-02-30, while accepting a fully cited observation with a real calendar date.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed validateRecObservation returns no error when field/value are absent, validateRecProvenance applies only ISO_DATE.test, and the dispatched test asserts that source-only provenance is accepted.

findings.title: Opt-in allowlist leaves detector recommendations without structured provenance
findings.what: The validator treats recommendations outside PROVENANCE_DETECTORS as compliant without provenance. These three dispatched detectors emit quantitative or historical claims but no observations, inference, or asOf block, preventing artifact/field-level reproduction and stale-signal demotion.
findings.fix: Require valid provenance for every emitted recommendation and add these detector IDs plus trigger fixtures; each detector should cite its parsed artifact fields and provide an asOf date for historical inputs.
findings.acceptance: Trigger tests for all three detectors assert non-empty field-level observations, valid inference/asOf data, and validateRecommendationProvenance returns no errors; a recommendation without provenance is rejected regardless of ID.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed the validator's explicit non-allowlisted exemption and re-read every return object in the three dispatched detectors; none contains provenance. The report-card object claims tallies/rates, api-errors claims counts/statuses, and config-drift claims dated event counts.

findings.title: Config-drift recency and evidence filters can produce unsupported findings
findings.what: The recency predicate has no upper bound, so an event timestamp later than now is included and described as occurring in the last seven days. Evidence is built only from warning events, so an info-only drift recommendation reports affected events while returning an empty evidence array.
findings.fix: Filter events with finite timestamps satisfying cutoff <= timestamp && timestamp <= now, and build capped evidence from all included projectEvents, prioritizing warnings if desired.
findings.acceptance: A unit test proves a future event does not fire; another proves an info-only appeared/vanished event emits a timestamped evidence row matching the counted event.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed projectEvents checks only timestamp >= cutoff, while evidence exclusively maps warnings. The existing info-only fixture establishes a reproducible path where warnings is empty but a recommendation is emitted.
